raw_evidence.quote:
Exit code
When there are some errors in diagrams the command returns an error (-1) exit code. But even if some diagrams contain some errors, all diagrams are generated, which can be time consuming for large project. You can use the -failfast flag to change this behavior to stop diagram generations as soon as one error occurs. In that case, some diagrams will be generated, and some will not. There is also a -failfast2 flag that does a first checking pass. If some error is present, no diagram will be generated at all. In case of error, -failfast2 runs even faster than -failfast, which may be useful for huge project.

--check-syntax ............... Check diagram syntax without generating images
--stop-on-error .............. Stop at the first syntax error
--check-before-run ........... Pre-check syntax of all inputs and stop faster on error
--no-error-image ............. Do not generate error images for diagrams with syntax errors

Using the -stdrpt (standard report) option, you can change the format of the error output of your PlantUML scripts. ... Without any option
java -jar plantuml.jar file1.pu
The error output is:
Error line 2 in file: file1.pu
Some diagram description contains errors

Exit codes:
0 Success
>0 Error (syntax error or processing failure)
See also: java -jar plantuml.jar --help-more

Exit codes:
0 Success
50 No file found
100 No diagram found in file(s)
200 Some diagrams have syntax errors

Param name | Short param name | Output format | Comment
--png | -f png | PNG | Default
--svg | -f svg | SVG | Vector graphics — use for web and documentation

# Check syntax only (CI)
java -jar plantuml.jar --check-syntax src/diagrams
# Read from stdin and write to stdout (SVG)
cat diagram.puml | java -jar plantuml.jar --svg -pipe > out.svg

validator_exists_and_exit_code_on_malfor.citation: plantuml.com/command-line §'Exit code' ('the command returns an error (-1) exit code') and 'New command-line interface (beta)' §'Exit codes:' (0/50/100/200 scheme)
validator_exists_and_exit_code_on_malfor.rationale: This directly answers the tension flagged in the assignment: PlantUML is documented to exit non-zero on a syntax error by default (legacy CLI: -1; new CLI: 200 for 'some diagrams have syntax errors'), so it is not simply 'error image, exit 0' behaviour. It is not, however, a semantic validator — see the separate finding below about what it does NOT check. --check-syntax additionally lets a caller validate without generating any image at all, and --no-error-image lets a caller suppress the error image while still getting the non-zero exit — both are documented flags that make a deterministic CI gate practical.

semantic_validation_beyond_syntax.citation: No flag or behaviour on this page (nor on the ie-diagram/er-diagram pages in the companion notation record) describes checking referential integrity, duplicate attribute names, or any cross-cutting convention
semantic_validation_beyond_syntax.rationale: Every documented error-handling flag (--check-syntax, --stop-on-error, --check-before-run, -failfast, -failfast2, -stdrpt) is framed in terms of 'syntax error' / 'diagram description contains errors' — i.e. grammar-level parse failure. Nothing in the command-line reference describes checking that a relationship references a previously-declared entity, that an attribute name is not duplicated within an entity, or that any cross-cutting convention (e.g. domain_id present on every table) holds. Because PlantUML's IE/Chen support sits on top of the general class-diagram engine, and class diagrams are documented elsewhere to auto-create a class/entity the first time its name is used in a relation (a well-known PlantUML behaviour for undeclared classes), the working assumption — not directly evidenced on this specific page and therefore recorded as an evidence gap — is that referencing an undeclared entity in a relation is not rejected but silently draws an empty box for it. This assumption is NOT independently confirmed against the parser source and is flagged as an unresolved gap below.

svg_png_export_flags.citation: plantuml.com/command-line, 'Output Format' table (--svg / -f svg; --png / -f png, default) and the CLI examples block ('cat diagram.puml | java -jar plantuml.jar --svg -pipe > out.svg')
svg_png_export_flags.rationale: SVG and PNG export are both documented first-class CLI output formats with exact flags (--svg, --png, or -f svg / -f png), including a piped stdin-to-stdout mode. Combined with the Dockerfile evidence in the companion GitHub-repo/licence-governance record (ENTRYPOINT java -jar plantuml.jar), this supports running 'docker run ... plantuml/plantuml --svg /data/file.puml' or '--png' with no local install, directly analogous to factory/scripts/structurizr's export-svg/export-png subcommands.

contrary_evidence_search.result: Confirmed (raw quote captured): PlantUML's default legacy-CLI exit code on a diagram containing errors is -1 (non-zero), and error images are generated by default unless --no-error-image is passed. NOT found: any documentation of semantic checks (undeclared-entity references, duplicate attributes, cross-cutting conventions). The behaviour for an undeclared entity referenced in a relation (silently auto-created as an empty box vs. rejected) is a known general PlantUML class-diagram behaviour from general familiarity with the tool, but this specific command-line reference page does not state it explicitly for IE/ER diagrams, so it is recorded as an UNRESOLVED GAP rather than a cited fact — a primary-source citation for this specific behaviour on ER/IE entities was not located within this session's time budget.
